In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the power sharing is not a problem as such but it may be a problem if it is not well understood and taken into account in the design of a power converter.
the IGBT-module should be operated with a low number of parallel chips, in order to avoid unbalances, and with a large number of parallel chips in order to reduce the thermal gradients in the module.
power sharing unbalances are not critical for the reliability of the IGBT-module.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the unbalances observed during transient operation are due to the non-identical behaviour of the chips in the IGBT-modules, which are not compensated by the parallel operation, and that they may lead to an increased stress of the individual chips, thus reducing the reliability of the IGBT-module.
the power-sharing unbalances are a consequence of the thermal resistance of the IGBT module, which is not uniform across the module.
a thorough investigation of the power sharing between the IGBTs is necessary for a reliable design of power converters used for traction applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the power distribution in a parallel-connected chip set is not uniform, and that the power sharing is affected by the thermal and electrical characteristics of the chips.
unbalances are a significant source of stress and degradation for the IGBTs, and that they should be considered in the design and optimization of traction converters.
unbalances can be reduced by a proper design of the module, and by an adequate thermal management.
